UnitStatement: Chirality closes the identified gap by implementing epistemic concepts as architectural invariants.
Chirality distinguishes model-level epistemic reliability from governance-level epistemic transparency.
Model-level epistemic reliability improves the probability that an LLM produces accurate outputs.
Model-level reliability approaches include RLHF, RAG, fine-tuning, and factuality verification.
Model-level epistemic reliability is the dominant approach in the current literature.
Governance-level epistemic transparency makes the epistemic status of every claim architecturally visible and auditable.
Governance-level epistemic transparency is independent of the model's underlying reliability.
Model-level approaches reduce the frequency of epistemic failures.
Governance-level approaches make epistemic failures detectable when they occur.
Governance-level approaches make the absence of grounding structurally observable even when no failure has occurred.
Professional engineering practice requires a licensed professional to judge the epistemic basis of every relied-upon claim.
A licensed professional's judgment about claim grounding cannot be delegated to a probabilistic model.
Professional reliance on AI-assisted work requires an architectural record of claim epistemic basis.
Chirality enforces K-PROV-1 as mandatory provenance across all agents.
Chirality enforces K-INVENT-1 as a no-invention invariant across all agents.
Chirality enforces K-CONFLICT-1 as conflict surfacing across all agents.
Chirality enforces the FACT/ASSUMPTION/PROPOSAL/TBD label system across all agents.
Chirality compliance is verifiable by inspection of the filesystem.
